```lean
CategoryTheory.abelianOfAdjunction.{v, u₁, u₂} {C : Type u₁} [Category.{v, u₁} C] [Preadditive C] [HasFiniteProducts C]
  {D : Type u₂} [Category.{v, u₂} D] [Abelian D] (F : C ⥤ D) [F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] (G : D ⥤ C)
  [G.PreservesZeroMorphisms] [PreservesFiniteLimits G] (i : F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 C) (adj : G ⊣ F) : Abelian C
```
***
If `C` is an additive category, `D` is an abelian category,
we have `F : C ⥤ D` `G : D ⥤ C` (both preserving zero morphisms),
`G` is left exact (that is, preserves finite limits),
and further we have `adj : G ⊣ F` and `i : F ⋙ G ≅ 𝟭 C`,
then `C` is also abelian.

See <https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03A3>
